text: The Patriots' trip to Jacksonville turned into a full-scale reckoning this past Sunday, as Drake Maye's early-season struggles reached a nadir in the team's humbling 35-6 loss to the Jaguars, with the second-year quarterback coughing up two interceptions and a fumble while watching Trevor Lawrence dissect New England's defense with three touchdown passes. Maye himself wasn't shy about assigning blame, calling both the offense's and his own performance "unacceptable" in the aftermath, signaling a level of self-awareness that will be crucial if the Patriots hope to arrest their downward trajectory, though questions are already mounting about whether the offense is being deployed in a way that allows Maye to succeed. The one bright spot came from cornerback Marcus Jones, who recorded his first interception of the season, a reminder that at least some elements of the defense are functioning, even as Jacksonville's coach Liam Coen got exactly the kind of response he'd been preaching all week from his team.
